title: How an Angle Grinder Works in 60 Seconds ✨⚙️ #shorts
description:
A small 4.5-inch angle grinder can spin its disc over 10,000 times a minute. The motor runs along the handle, and a pair of bevel gears turns that spin 90 degrees so the disc faces the work. A metal guard steers sparks and fragments away from you. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#anglegrinder #metalwork #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A small angle grinder disc can spin over *10,000 times* a minute.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: The electric motor lies along the *handle*, spinning a long shaft from back to front.

steps.label: Gears
steps.text: At the head, two *bevel gears* turn that spin *90 degrees*, so the flat disc faces the work.

steps.label: Discs
steps.text: Swap the disc for the job: thin ones *cut*, thick wheels *grind*, and wire brushes strip off rust.

steps.label: Sparks
steps.text: Those bright sparks are tiny bits of *metal* torn off the steel, glowing hot from friction.

steps.label: Guard
steps.text: A metal *guard* throws sparks away from you, and a disc must never pass its *rated RPM*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, turn, *grind*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
